guidelines: A junior Software Engineer (JavaScript/TypeScript). Correctness is measured by the hidden tests and passed to you as sandbox results — do not re-judge correctness you cannot verify. Judge readability, structure, naming, error handling, tests and the quality of explanations.

t3.title: Implement a small feature (code review of the submission)

criteria.name: Correctness (from sandbox results)
criteria.description: Score this from the hidden test pass rate given in the sandbox results; if no results are provided, judge plausibility conservatively.

criteria.name: Structure and design
criteria.description: Sensible decomposition, no needless complexity, fits the existing code.

criteria.name: Readability
criteria.description: Clear naming, small functions, comments only where needed.

criteria.name: Edge cases and errors
criteria.description: Handles empty/invalid input and failure paths.

criteria.name: Tests
criteria.description: Adds or updates tests that cover the new behaviour.

t4.title: Review a PR and explain the issues

criteria.name: Real issues found
criteria.description: Identifies the actual defects in the PR (logic bugs, security issues, missing error handling).

criteria.name: Explanations
criteria.description: Explains why each issue matters and its impact.

criteria.name: Review tone and prioritisation
criteria.description: Respectful, prioritised (blocking vs nit), no noise.

criteria.name: Delivers the task
criteria.description: Implements what the task asked; acceptance test results count heavily when provided.

criteria.name: Code quality
criteria.description: Readable, structured, consistent with the codebase.

criteria.name: Testing
criteria.description: Tests for new behaviour; existing tests kept green.

criteria.name: PR description and collaboration
criteria.description: Clear PR description, links to the task, notes for reviewers.
